Vyshnivets Kvoresl Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopil Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Vyshnivets's Jewish community, first settled in the mid-16th century, suffered during the 1653 Tatar invasion but grew to a peak of 3,178 people by 1847, supported by five synagogues and a Talmud Torah by 1863; a Jewish self-defense group successfully staved off violence during the Russian Civil War. By the 1930s, the town supported eight synagogues and an operating yeshiva, with Jews numbering around 3,000 (60 percent) by 1937. This cemetery, mentioned and mapped in the 1970 Yizkor memorial book 'Sefer Vishnevets,' was demolished after WWII, per local testimony. Following the July 1941 Wehrmacht occupation, more than 400 Jews were murdered, and a ghetto established in March 1942 held 3,500 people, including Jews from neighboring villages; its August 11, 1942 liquidation saw about 2,500 Jews executed.
